title: Code Reviewer environment control, version 1
description: #975, epic #969, ADR 0005: the environment control of a Worker, the one interface through which Control asks whoever started the sandbox to change the sandbox's outer network wall (`narrow`) and tells it that the Worker ended (`report_end`). The Worker (runner/src/code_reviewer_runner/implementer/environment_control.py) has two transports and the environment it is started with chooses one. `https`: the hosted Dispatcher's `POST /network` (docs/dispatcher.md), chosen by `RUNNER_IMPLEMENTER_NETWORK_SWITCH`, unchanged on the wire and not described here. `vsock` (this file): chosen by `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT_CONTROL=vsock`, used by vm-init of a Firecracker VM on a customer's own Linux machine (#977) and answered by the local Dispatcher (#978, #979). With neither variable the Worker runs with the inner wall (the network door) only and says so once. THE VSOCK TRANSPORT. The Worker opens one stream connection of the address family AF_VSOCK to the host (`ControlHostCid`, 2) on `ControlPort` for every request and closes it after the reply. A message is a frame: four bytes, the length of the body as an unsigned big-endian number (1 to `ControlMaxFrameBytes`), then the body, one UTF-8 JSON object that is valid under `ControlRequest` (Worker to host) or `ControlReply` (host to Worker), closed, with `version` 1. A length of 0 or above the limit, a body that is not one such object, a version other than 1, a type the receiver does not know and any byte after the one frame of a request are protocol errors: the receiver closes the connection without an answer (a host MAY first send a `refused` reply with the reason `invalid_request`). A side that waits for the other waits at most `ControlNarrowSeconds` for `narrow` and `ControlEndSeconds` for `end` (connect included) and then gives up; the Worker ends the job with the error code `environment_control_failed` when `narrow` times out, is refused, or the host cannot be reached, and ignores any failure of `end`. THE HOST'S DUTY. It answers `narrow` with `ack` only after the outer wall holds the job's rule, so that the agent never starts under the setup's wide rule, and answers a rule it does not allow with `refused` (`rule_not_allowed`). Both requests are idempotent: the host answers the same request again the same way. The connection is the VM's own (a Firecracker vsock device is made for one VM), so the host knows which VM and job a request belongs to and nothing in a message names one; a host that serves more than one VM keeps them apart by the connection and never by a field here. THE TOKEN (additive, still version 1: `token` is optional in the schema, a host that serves a VM of vm-init requires it). The host makes a random `ControlToken` for each VM and sends it in the start; Control receives it on its stdin with its credential (never in an argument, the environment or a log) and puts it in every `narrow` and `end` it sends. A host checks it with the helper of `dispatcher/src/launchers/control-token.ts` and refuses a request without it or with another: what the agent can open of AF_VSOCK is closed by seccomp as defence in depth, the token is what the host trusts. A Worker that has none (not started by vm-init) sends none and is refused by such a host.

ControlVariable.description: The environment variable that chooses the vsock transport; its one value is `ControlTransportValue`. The Worker refuses a container that sets it to anything else, and one that sets it next to `RUNNER_IMPLEMENTER_NETWORK_SWITCH` (the https transport), with `implementer_config_invalid`. It holds no secret and is set by whoever starts the Worker container (vm-init, #977).

ControlHostCid.description: The context id of the host in the VM's AF_VSOCK address space (VMADDR_CID_HOST).

ControlPort.description: The vsock port the host's environment control listens on (Firecracker maps it to the file `<vsock uds path>_5100` of the host).

ControlMaxFrameBytes.description: The most bytes a frame's body has. The largest message is a `narrow` request with a list rule of 100 host names of 253 characters, about 27,000 bytes.

ControlNarrowSeconds.description: How long the Worker waits for the answer to `narrow`, from the connect to the end of the reply.

ControlEndSeconds.description: How long the Worker waits for the answer to `end`; the Worker is ending, so it is short.

ControlNetworkRule.description: The rule for the agent's network, the same as `ImplementerNetworkRule` of the runner API (`off`: nothing, `list`: the host names in `hosts`, each exact or `*.` and a suffix, `open`: any public name; `hosts` is empty unless the mode is `list`). `ports` is the Worker's own narrowing of the ports the network door dials and is present only when it is not both of them.

ControlToken.description: The per-VM token of the host (#977 fix round): 32 to 96 random bytes in base64url without padding, made by the host for one VM and sent to vm-init in the start (`controlToken` of `vm-init.v1.json`), to Control on its stdin and from there in every request of this file. It is the one thing that tells the host a message is the Worker's and not a forged one: `AF_VSOCK` is closed to the agent by the container's seccomp profile, which is defence in depth, and the token is what the host trusts. The host compares it in constant time, refuses a request without it or with another one (`refused`, `invalid_request`, or the connection closed) and never logs it.

NarrowRequest.description: Worker to host: switch the outer wall from the setup's wide rule to the job's: GitHub, the app, the model provider's host (`modelHost`, a plain lower-case ASCII host name, never an address or a wildcard) and `network`. Sent once, after the setup script ended and before the agent exists.

EndRequest.description: Worker to host: the Worker ends with this exit code (0 ok, 1 the job failed, 2 setup error); the host may power the sandbox off once it answered. Best effort: the Worker does not wait for more than `ControlEndSeconds` and ignores a refusal.

ControlRequest.description: A frame from the Worker to the host.

ControlRequestType.description: The `type` of a request, and the `for` of the reply that answers it.

ControlRefusalReason.description: Why a host refused: `rule_not_allowed` (the rule or the model host is not one this host lets a job have), `invalid_request` (the request is well formed JSON but not a request of this contract), `unavailable` (the host cannot do it now, for example its proxy does not answer). A Worker branches on the code and never on anything else.

AckReply.description: Host to Worker: the request named in `for` is done (for `narrow`, the outer wall holds the rule).

RefusedReply.description: Host to Worker: the request named in `for` was not done, and asking again will not change that.

ControlReply.description: A frame from the host to the Worker.
